name: HI-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+12 district in deeply Democratic Hawaii
Tokuda's overwhelming cash advantage: $570K on hand vs $16K for Awa
No outside spending against Tokuda and no polling indicating a contest
Prediction markets price Tokuda's re-election around 96%
model.rationale: Tokuda combines a D+12 seat, incumbency, and a roughly seven-to-one cash-on-hand advantage, while no outside groups are opposing her and Awa has raised little money. Markets price her near certain re-election, consistent with a Safe Democratic rating.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Awa within single digits or new Republican outside spending would be the main signal to revisit this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Hawaii's second district is firmly Democratic territory, and incumbent Jill Tokuda enters the general election with the advantages that usually decide races here. She has raised more than $820,000 and holds over $570,000 in cash, while Republican Brenton Awa has raised about $123,000 with just $16,000 available. No outside groups are spending against Tokuda or on Awa's behalf.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on the district's D+12 lean, Tokuda's incumbency, and the money gap. Prediction markets put her chances around 96 percent. Awa would need an unusually favorable turnout pattern to close a deficit of this size. The seat is rated Safe Democratic, with the main question being the final margin rather than the winner.
